phenomenon: idiom: back to the drawing board
prompt: My team lead looked at our prototype and said 'back to the drawing board'. In one sentence, what does she want us to do?

costar.context: A team member asks what a team lead's idiomatic reaction to a prototype means.
costar.objective: Explain that 'back to the drawing board' means the design has failed and the team must start the design again from the beginning.
costar.audience: A team member who received the feedback.

reference: She means the prototype does not work as it is, so you need to start the design again from the beginning.

candidates.A: She is saying the current version has failed and the team should rethink the whole design from scratch.
candidates.B: She means the prototype is good, so you need to take it back to the drawing board in the office and start drawing the final version.
candidates.C: lol she hated it, bin the thing and start over mate

phenomenon: register: explaining a delay to a customer
prompt: A customer emailed asking why her sofa delivery is late. It is stuck at the port and should arrive next Tuesday. Write a two-sentence reply.

costar.context: A furniture shop replies by email to a customer whose sofa delivery is late because the shipment is held at the port.
costar.objective: Explain the cause of the delay and give the new expected delivery date of next Tuesday.
costar.audience: A customer who is waiting for her order.

reference: We are sorry that your sofa is late: the shipment is currently held at the port. We expect it to reach you next Tuesday, and we will confirm the delivery time with you beforehand.

candidates.A: Please accept our apologies for the delay, which is caused by a hold-up with the shipment at the port. Your sofa should now arrive next Tuesday, and we will confirm the exact time with you in advance.
candidates.B: We are sorry that your sofa is late: the shipment is currently held at the port. We expect it to reach you next Thursday, and we will confirm the delivery time with you beforehand.
